newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK ferry in collision, all on board rescued unhurt.
newsitem.headline: HK ferry in collision, all on board rescued unhurt.

text.p: A high-speed ferry bound for the south China city of Zhuhai from Hong Kong collided with a smaller vessel on Wednesday, but all its passengers and crew were rescued unhurt, the Hong Kong Marine Department said.
A total of 193 passengers and eight crew were on board the ferry at the time of the collision.
The catamaran Hoi Bin, which had sailed from Hong Kong's Victoria Harbour, collided with a small vessel west of the island of Shek Kwu Chau, the department said in a statement.
The collision tore a hole measuring two metres by 1.5 metres in Hoi Bin's bow above the waterline, it said.
The captain of the smaller vessel, with two crew members and three passengers on board, was slightly injured and admitted to hospital, it said. The smaller boat sustained only minor damage.
Of the catamaran's passengers, 188 boarded another vessel sent by the ferry operator, Chu Kong Shipping Co Ltd, and continued across the Pearl River delta to Zhuhai.
The other five passengers chose to return to Hong Kong by police launch.
The Marine Department said it was investigating the cause of the collision.
